Broadcasting to Rooms

notifyRealtime.listener.js sends the same four domain events to whichever room each one is relevant to, wired up from server.js.

// Figure 5.14: the realtime channel's take on ticket.created (src/events/listeners/notifyRealtime.listener.js, excerpt)
domainEvents.on(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, (ticket) => {
  try {
    const io = getIO();
    if (!io) return;

    io.to(`user:${ticket.customerId}`).emit(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, ticket);
    io.to('role:agent').emit(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, ticket);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('notifyRealtime listener failed for ticket.created:', err);
  }
});

Same domainEvents.on(...) shape as the previous two channels, reacting to the same event, in a third file that knows nothing about either of them. io.to(room).emit(...) is the broadcast half of the previous slide's rooms: ticket.created reaches the customer's own room and the shared agent room in two lines, with no loop over individual connections. getIO() returning undefined — true whenever nothing has called initSocket(), notably every test that imports app.js directly through supertest without ever starting a real server — makes this listener return quietly rather than throw, so tests exercising createTicket don't need a real Socket.IO server running at all.

That getIO() only ever returns something because server.js, not app.js, creates the real HTTP server Socket.IO needs and initializes it:

// Figure 5.15: a real http.Server, so Socket.IO has something to attach to (src/server.js, excerpt)
const httpServer = http.createServer(app);
initSocket(httpServer);

httpServer.listen(env.PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Support Desk API listening on http://localhost:${env.PORT}`);
});

app.listen(...) — what every earlier lesson used — actually creates an http.Server internally and hides it; Socket.IO needs to attach to that server object directly, so it's created explicitly here instead, wrapping the same Express app. This is the same reasoning as app.js/server.js being split in the first place: app.js stays a plain Express app with no opinion about sockets or ports, and only server.js — never touched by supertest — knows a real server, and a real Socket.IO instance, exist at all.
